questions.stem:
Statements: No bonds is a deposits. Some deposits are cheques. All cheques are lockers.
Conclusions:
I. All bonds are lockers.
II. Some lockers are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some bonds are deposits. All deposits are cheques. No cheques is a lockers.
Conclusions:
I. Some bonds are cheques.
II. Some deposits are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few bonds are deposits. Some deposits are cheques. All cheques are lockers.
Conclusions:
I. All bonds are lockers.
II. No deposits is a lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few bonds are deposits. All deposits are cheques. No cheques is a lockers.
Conclusions:
I. Some bonds are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: W < P < S > V < T.
Conclusions: I. S < P   II. P > T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. W ≤ S   II. X ≥ S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural credit digital = mi lu vo
rural growth banking = ka ze lu
credit growth secure = su ze vo
digital banking secure = ka mi su
rural credit secure = vo lu su
What is the code for “digital”?
questions.explanation: Answer: mi. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = lu, credit = vo, digital = mi, growth = ze, banking = ka, secure = su.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 28 km north, turns right and walks 32 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 24 km along the initial direction and 32 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 88 km north, turns right and walks 120 km, then turns right and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 136. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 64 km along the initial direction and 120 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(64² + 120²) = 136 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 86 km west, turns right and walks 156 km, then turns right and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 169. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 65 km along the initial direction and 156 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(65² + 156²) = 169 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of E. H is the son of E. D is the father of E. How is H related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. D is a parent of E, and H is E’s son. Hence H is D’s grandchild.

questions.stem: H is the brother of C. C is the mother of D. G is the father of H and C. How is H related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. H is the brother of D’s mother C. Therefore H is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: C is the only daughter of H. H is the father of C. E is the son of C. B is the sister of H. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. H is the father of C, and C is E’s mother. Thus H is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 54 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 38. New front rank = 14+3 = 17. Back rank = 54 − 17 + 1 = 38.

questions.stem: In a queue of 39 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1750. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2613.33. Selling price = 1750 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 2613.33.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 22 days and B in 33 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 18.67. Use 66 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 66 − 2×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 112 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 11 km/h and stream speed is 3 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹15000 for 12 months. B invests ₹60000 for 4 months. Total profit is ₹103600. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 59200. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 16. B’s share = total × 16/(28) = 59200.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹21000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 210. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 21000 × (10/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 16. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 16.

questions.stem: The average of 28 numbers is 68. One number, 80, is replaced and the average rises by 6. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 248. Total increases by 28 × 6. New number = 80 + 168.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 8 years, their combined age will be 72 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 16 = 72; x = 14, so father = 42.
